newsitem.title: CUBA: Canada sends aid for Cuban hurricane victims.
newsitem.headline: Canada sends aid for Cuban hurricane victims.

text.p: Canada, a key trading partner of Cuba, on Wednesday sent a planeload of relief aid for Cubans hard hit by Hurricane Lili this month.

A Canadian Air Force C-130 transport plane arrived at Havana airport with water purification tablets, blankets and rehydration salts donated by the Canadian Red Cross. The aid will be distributed by the Cuban Red Cross.

Cuban Red Cross officials said the cargo would be distributed in the next few days in the provinces of Matanzas, Cienfuegos and Villa Clara. Cuban authorities have said the hurricane, which swept through central and western areas of Cuba on Oct. 17-18, destroyed about 5,000 homes and damaged crops, power lines and communications lines.

Canada's relief effort follows donations from other countries. Mexico has sent several planeloads of food and roofing materials and Spain has promised $200,000 worth of assistance. The European Union said this week it was giving about $800,000 to help hurricane victims.

The Cuban American community, mostly in Florida, also mobilised to send aid and the U.S. government last week waived a ban on direct flights to allow a planeload of food channelled through a Roman Catholic church charity to be flown to Havana on Saturday. But church sources said on Wednesday the cargo still had not been transported to Cienfuegos, where it was meant to be distributed, because of logistical hold-ups.

Cuba, hit by the hurricane at a time when it was slowly emerging from a five-year economic crisis, has appealed to the United Nations for humanitarian assistance. Diplomatic sources said Havana has also asked at least five countries -- France, Brazil, Canada, Italy and Britain -- for credits to help tide it over a foreign exhcange squeeze.
